review_basis: Direct independent access to primary pages listed below; IDs reused only where title and URL match the investigator source-map exactly. S-SQLITE-ATTACH-ATOMICITY is new.

sources.title: SQLite FTS5 Extension
sources.version_or_commit: Living official documentation accessed 2026-10-12; feature condition noted: contentless-delete tables available since SQLite 3.43.0; shipped runtime remains unknown.
sources.locator: Sections 3, 4.3.1, 4.3.4, 4.4.1–4.4.3, 6.12 and 6.13; query grammar, unicode61, trigram, contentless update/delete restrictions, external-content synchronization, rebuild and secure-delete.
sources.observed_operation: Opened official documentation; checked default tokenizer and options, ordinary/contentless-delete table operations, same-database external-content behavior, rebuild and deleted-term retention.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: unicode61 is default and based on Unicode 6.1; external content must be synchronized by the caller. Ordinary contentless tables cannot use normal UPDATE/DELETE/REPLACE; the FTS5 delete command is available. Contentless-delete behavior is a newer option. Rebuild deletes and reconstructs the index and is unavailable for contentless tables. Trigram full-text matches require at least three Unicode characters. The contentless delete command requires the original indexed column values and rowid; contentless-delete tables support delete by rowid but have their own version/operation conditions.
sources.applicability: Supports the proposal’s SQLite tradeoffs and the critic’s C-01 caveat. The candidate runtime/build and table mode are unknown.

sources.title: SQLite Write-Ahead Logging
sources.locator: Sections 1 and 2; reader/writer concurrency and WAL commit behavior.
sources.observed_operation: Opened official WAL documentation and checked writer concurrency and checkpoint context.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Readers and a writer can run concurrently, but only one writer at a time; checkpointing has separate progress considerations.
sources.applicability: Relevant only if the target notebook uses SQLite/WAL; the target store is not identified.

sources.title: SQLite ATTACH DATABASE
sources.locator: Transactions involving multiple attached databases, paragraph at the end of the page.
sources.observed_operation: Opened official documentation and checked the crash-atomicity condition for multi-database transactions.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Cross-database transactions are atomic if main is not :memory: and journal_mode is not WAL; under WAL or an in-memory main database each file is individually atomic but a host crash during commit can leave files inconsistent.
sources.applicability: Supports the draft’s conservative sidecar/outbox warning; does not establish the target app’s journal mode or transaction design.

sources.title: SQLite forum: external-content FTS5 with nested AFTER UPDATE trigger writes
sources.version_or_commit: Maintainer/forum record dated 2026-08-04/05; page reports reproductions including SQLite 3.53.2; no formal release fix identified in this record.
sources.locator: Corrected reproducer and workaround, posts/sections describing two AFTER UPDATE triggers and nested same-table UPDATE.
sources.observed_operation: Opened record, checked the minimal trigger combination, expected/actual behavior and suggested workaround.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The reported corruption requires an external-content FTS5 sync trigger plus another same-table AFTER UPDATE trigger that issues a nested UPDATE; this is a specific trigger-graph report, not a general external-content failure.
sources.applicability: Supports inspecting the target trigger graph if FTS5 external-content mode is evaluated.

sources.title: SQLite forum: FTS5 Unicode61 Polish ł/Ł
sources.version_or_commit: Historical user/maintainer discussion; reporter used SQLite 3.30.1; maintainer response 2021-01-11.
sources.locator: Posts 1–3; UnicodeData mapping discussion and custom-tokenizer suggestion.
sources.observed_operation: Opened forum record and checked the reporter example and maintainer explanation.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The issue illustrates that remove_diacritics does not map ł/Ł to plain l as expected in the report because its Unicode decomposition differs; it is historical behavior evidence, not a guarantee about every future runtime.
sources.applicability: Useful as a proposed language fixture; does not establish a supported-language decision.

sources.title: SQLite forum: Crash in FTS5 Module
sources.version_or_commit: Forum report from 2024-08; fix confirmation names SQLite 3.46.1.
sources.locator: Posts 1, 3 and 4; malformed option reproducer, trunk error behavior and 3.46.1 release confirmation.
sources.observed_operation: Opened maintainer/forum record and checked exact malformed configuration and stated fix release.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The report concerns missing option values for trigram case_sensitive/remove_diacritics on affected builds; the fix makes tokenizer construction return an error. Do not generalize this to valid configurations.
sources.applicability: Supports pinning/testing the runtime if optional trigram configuration is evaluated.

sources.title: SQLite Release History
sources.version_or_commit: Official release history, accessed 2026-10-12; relevant change is SQLite 3.46.1.
sources.locator: 3.46.1 tokenizer-argument parsing robustness entry, cross-referenced by the SQLite forum record.
sources.observed_operation: Opened release-history page; the specific fix statement was directly checked in the linked forum confirmation as well.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Release note is about robust parsing of FTS5 tokenize= arguments; it is not evidence of the app’s shipped SQLite version.
sources.applicability: Version-gate candidate tokenizer features and configuration against the actual build.

sources.version_or_commit: Tantivy release tag 0.26.2 named by the exact release URL; full commit hash not independently captured.
sources.observed_operation: Opened version-pinned official release page to confirm the candidate version named by the API and example URLs.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The pinned docs/example apply to Tantivy crate/repository tag 0.26.2, not a future or unpinned dependency.

sources.title: Tantivy 0.26.2 IndexWriter API
sources.locator: IndexWriter commit, delete_term and add_document API sections.
sources.observed_operation: Opened version-pinned API docs and checked commit visibility/persistence, delete visibility, and add pipeline blocking conditions.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: commit blocks and publishes/persists pending documents; deletes become visible on commit; add_document may block if the indexing pipeline is full.
sources.applicability: Supports bounded background writer and post-commit acknowledgement as a proposed design; target workload and operating systems still need evaluation.

sources.title: Tantivy 0.26.2 tokenizer module
sources.locator: default tokenizer, en_stem, and custom-tokenizer sections.
sources.observed_operation: Opened version-pinned tokenizer documentation and checked default split/filter behavior, English stemming and custom-tokenizer extension.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Default splits on punctuation/whitespace, removes tokens longer than 40 characters and lowercases; en_stem adds stemming, is slower than default, and is described as useful for recall; custom tokenizers are supported.
sources.applicability: Supports the proposal’s conditional tokenizer comparison, not a multilingual quality claim.

sources.title: Tantivy 0.26.2 deleting/updating documents example
sources.version_or_commit: Repository tag 0.26.2 named by the exact versioned example URL; full commit hash not independently captured.
sources.locator: Example comments and schema around lines 561–600; update/delete and commit/reload example around lines 656–708.
sources.observed_operation: Opened version-pinned example and checked its explicit primary-ID limitation and stable indexed ID example.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The example says Tantivy has no primary-ID notion; an indexed field can serve as an ID. App-side uniqueness, canonical-store synchronization and title/body storage policy remain responsibilities.
sources.applicability: Supports using an app-owned stable ID in a Tantivy candidate; it does not prove the actual product store has such IDs.

draft_source_id_policy: Same identifiers from investigator source-map.json are reused only for the same source title/URL. This map records sources independently reopened by the critic; it does not silently substitute a different source under an existing ID.
